headline: Methods refine isoform calling and quantification from long-read RNA-seq
label: Long Read Isoform Quantification Methods
summary: Long-read RNA-seq now resolves isoforms at scale, prompting new calling, quantification, and differential transcript usage benchmarks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is isoform-level resolution of transcriptomes, as long-read and single-cell sequencing move analysis beyond gene-level expression. Isocall performs deterministic joint transcript calling across many PacBio long-read samples, and Bramble projects spliced genomic alignments into transcriptomic space to improve abundance estimates. KuPID applies k-mer sketching as a prefilter for long reads, reporting 2-3x faster isoform discovery and F1 gains of up to 11.6 points. A real-data framework benchmarks differential transcript usage methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial data. A single-cell long-read isoform atlas across 26 human tissues reports isoform usage as an identity axis distinct from gene expression. Separately, RAISE infers RBP activity from CLIP-seq, motifs, and splicing changes, and a collision-aware UMI estimator indicates shorter UMIs can suffice for accurate quantification.
